For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). 3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to a substantive (not merely evidence-gathering) intervention? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

374	CASE OD2-DEV-INCOMPLETE (INCOMPLETE, cross-domain): Missed appointments after the scheduler change at Corrie Lane Outpatient Centre
375	Setting: Corrie Lane Outpatient Centre is one of two outpatient sites run by Hollins Vale Hospitals, a fictional regional hospital group. It runs orthopaedics, dermatology and endocrinology clinics, Monday to Friday, with about 2,900 appointments still booked on the day each month. On 3 March 2026 it moved from a legacy scheduler to Tidewell Scheduling, supplied by Osterline Systems. The sister site, Eastgate Outpatient Centre, is still on the legacy scheduler.
376	Presenting request: The operations director asks why the did-not-attend (DNA) rate at Corrie Lane has gone from about 8% to over 13% since the scheduler change, and what the hospital should do about it. The board wants a recommendation by November.
377	INITIAL EVIDENCE
378	E1 [stage S1] Email from Mairead Tolland, Director of Outpatient Operations, 9 Sept 2026 (leadership-account): Our did-not-attend (DNA) rate at Corrie Lane has gone from about 8% to over 13% since Tidewell went live on 3 March. The board wants an explanation and a fix by November. My view: the front desk stopped the day-before confirmation calls when the old system's printed call sheets went, and nobody told me. I'd like you to confirm that so I can deal with it through the team leads. Owen thinks it's partly the March cuts to the route 14 bus and partly that Tidewell 'counts differently'. Please tell us what is driving this and what we should do.
379	E2 [stage S1] Outpatient performance dashboard, Corrie Lane, extract 8 Sept 2026 (system-record): Monthly DNA rate (DNAs divided by appointments still booked on the day). Sep 2025 7.9%; Oct 8.3%; Nov 8.0%; Dec 8.7%; Jan 2026 7.6%; Feb 8.1% (mean 8.1%). Mar 2026: withheld; Apr 2026: withheld. May 13.1%; Jun 13.5%; Jul 13.6%; Aug 13.4% (mean 13.4%). Appointments booked on the day: 2,860–2,990 per month throughout. Footnote 1: March–April withheld until the outcomes of migrated appointments are reconciled. Footnote 2: according to the analytics team, month-to-month differences under 1 percentage point are normal variation at this volume.
380	E3 [stage S1] Change record CR-2026-0117, Tidewell go-live, Corrie Lane (change-record): Go-live 3 March 2026. All three specialties (orthopaedics, dermatology, endocrinology) switched over on the same day. Configuration: (1) Messaging. The legacy system sent one SMS 48 hours before each appointment. Tidewell sends a confirmation SMS at booking plus one reminder SMS at a fixed offset, set to 7 days (the vendor default). Tidewell allows one reminder offset per session template, and the vendor can change the offset for any template within two working days. (2) Booking. New and follow-up templates open 16 weeks ahead (legacy: 6 weeks). Follow-ups are booked at checkout instead of going on the recall list. (3) Outcome codes. The legacy code 'Arrived late – not seen' is mapped to Tidewell 'DNA'. Rollback: legacy system decommissioned 30 April.
381	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Bisi Adeyemi-Clarke, front-desk team lead, 12 Sept 2026 (staff-account): BA-C: 'We never stopped the calls. The day-before calls were always for the minor-procedures list, meaning skin ops and joint injections, so people know to stop blood thinners or arrange a lift home. Now I run that list from a Tidewell report instead of the old printout. What has changed is patients telling us at the desk that they didn't get "the text the day before" like they used to. And follow-ups now book their next appointment before they leave, sometimes four months out. Some of them look at the card and laugh.' Interviewer note: the director has asked BA-C to account for the call process, and she was visibly defensive.
382	E5 [stage S1] Patient Advice desk log, Corrie Lane, scheduling-related entries May–Aug 2026 (customer-account): Extracts (4 of 23 scheduling-related entries): (a) 'Used to get a text two days before. Now I get one a week before, and by the day I'd forgotten.' (b) 'Got a text the day I booked and one a week before, nothing nearer the time. Missed my endocrine review.' (c) 'Why are you texting me a week early? I nearly came on the wrong day.' (d) 'Was given an August date back in April. My shifts changed in the meantime and I couldn't get through on the phone to move it.' The other 19 entries: phone waiting times (11), car parking (5), other (3).
383	E6 [stage S1] Note from Owen Faraday, Clinic Manager, Corrie Lane, 10 Sept 2026 (manager-account): Honestly, I think a good chunk of this is Tidewell counting differently. The old system had a separate 'arrived late – not seen' code, and the migration lumped all of that into DNA. Until the data people sort out March and April, I'd suggest we stop sending the DNA figure to the board, because it makes us look worse than we are. The other thing is the bus. Vale Transit cut route 14 on 1 March, and a lot of our older patients rely on it.
384	CATALOGUE (full contents)
385	C1 [stage S1] Attended-visit billing reconciliation, Sep 2025–Aug 2026 - Hollins Vale Hospitals income team (financial-record): Billable attended outpatient visits matched to appointments still booked on the day. Sep–Feb (legacy): attended 91.6%, DNA 8.1%, 'arrived late – not seen' 0.3%. May–Aug (Tidewell): attended 86.6%, DNA (including late-not-seen) 13.4%. Booked-on-day volumes were similar (2,917 vs 2,902 per month), but attended visits fell from an average of 2,672 to 2,513 per month. Income team note: bills are generated from clinicians' encounter entries, not from the scheduler's outcome code. The late-not-seen remapping can account for at most about 0.3 points of the change.
386	C2 [stage S1] Clinical records audit of DNA-coded appointments, May–June 2026 - Clinical audit team (lead: R. Gilchrist) (independent-observation): Random sample of 200 Tidewell appointments coded DNA in May–June, checked against clinician notes, kiosk check-in logs and same-day pathology or imaging requests. 193 (96.5%): no evidence of attendance. 4 (2.0%): arrived late and not seen (the legacy system would have coded these 'late – not seen'). 3 (1.5%): attended and seen, outcome keyed wrongly. Audit conclusion: miscoded records make up about 3.5% of DNA codes, roughly 0.5 percentage points of the 13.4% rate. Miscoding does not explain a rise of the size reported.
387	C3 [stage S1] Monthly DNA rates, Eastgate Outpatient Centre (Sep 2025–Aug 2026) and Corrie Lane (May–Aug 2025) - Hollins Vale Hospitals analytics team (system-record): Eastgate Outpatient Centre: same hospital group; runs orthopaedics, dermatology and general medicine; stays on the legacy scheduler until 2027 (48-hour SMS reminder, 6-week booking horizon). About 60% of its catchment postcodes overlap with Corrie Lane's, and Vale Transit route 14 serves both sites. Eastgate DNA rate: Sep–Feb mean 7.9%; May–Aug 2026 mean 8.2% (May 8.0, Jun 8.3, Jul 8.4, Aug 8.1). Corrie Lane in the same months a year earlier (May–Aug 2025, legacy system): 7.8%, 8.0%, 8.3%, 8.1% (mean 8.1%).
388	C4 [stage S1] Outbound call records from front-desk telephone lines, January–August 2026 - Telephony platform export, extensions 4410–4414 (log): Outbound calls to patient numbers, weekly mean: Jan–Feb 91; May–Aug 88. Calls fell to 64 a week in March (cutover weeks) and were back to normal by mid-April. Matched against the minor-procedures list, the share of listed patients with a logged call 1–2 working days before their appointment was 93% in Jan–Feb and 91% in May–Aug. In both periods the only other outbound calls were ad-hoc rebooking calls (about 10 a week). SOP OP-22 (2023) requires day-before calls for the minor-procedures list only.
389	C5 [stage S1] Vale Transit service change notice, route 14, effective 1 March 2026 - Vale Transit public notice (external-data): Route 14 (Hollins Cross – Corrie Lane – Eastgate). From 1 March 2026, evening buses after 19:00 run every 60 minutes instead of every 30, and the Sunday service is withdrawn. Monday–Saturday service between 07:00 and 19:00 is unchanged at every 15 minutes. For reference, Corrie Lane outpatient sessions run 08:30–17:00, Monday to Friday, with the last appointments at 16:30.

rulings.explanation: A2 fits the definition of 'premature': it is right only if H1, which is still unconfirmed, is true. But the evidence also supports 'acceptable'. E3 and C11 say the change is free and can be reversed within two working days. External causes and artefact are ruled out (C1, C3, C5). The board deadline puts weight on acting. The key says A2 'removes the comparison', but that is weaker than it claims. A clinic-wide switch to 48 hours with booking practice held constant would still give a pre/post test of the reminder alone, with Eastgate as a concurrent control (C3). That is less clean than A1's randomisation but still informative. The cost the key cites, about 130 refilled slots a month (C12), can be undone as quickly as the switch, and C12 records no legacy refill figure to show the 7-day reminder actually gained anything. So an analyst could reasonably call A2 'reasonable but not among the best' rather than 'not justified'. Nothing in the evidence clearly separates 'premature' from 'acceptable'.
rulings.fix: Remove the 'cheap and quickly reversible' basis for 'acceptable'. Add to C11: 'An offset change applies only to reminders for appointments booked after the change; reminders for already-booked appointments (up to 16 weeks ahead) keep their original offset, so a clinic-wide switch takes about 16 weeks to take full effect and as long again to reverse.' Optionally add to the C12 addendum: 'most refilled slots go to patients on the 18-week breach list.' Together these make a clinic-wide commitment slow and costly to unwind, which makes 'premature' the only defensible answer.

rulings.explanation: The blind argument for 'sufficient' is to intervene on the 'scheduler configuration as a whole'. That is not a single action. Rollback is impossible because the legacy system was decommissioned on 30 April (E3). So in practice it means doing both A2 and A3 clinic-wide. That would knowingly incur both documented costs: lost early-cancellation refills, and dependence on recall-clerk staffing (C12). It would also give up learning which mechanism is operating (C6–C10 show none of the data can separate them). Knowing that Tidewell's configuration is implicated (C1, C3) does not tell you which part to change, and C14 only rules out a change in patient mix. 'Do nothing' is ruled out because the problem is real. The board deadline can be met with A1: an 8-week test started in mid-September ends in mid-November. So the evidence is insufficient to commit to a substantive intervention, and 'insufficient' is the only defensible answer.

By the definitions, 'unknown' means the evidence is insufficient even to show association, while 'association-only' means the factors co-occur or correlate but causation is not established. Both exposures clearly co-occur with the step rise in DNA. E3 and C6 show the 48-hour SMS was removed on 3 March across all templates. C7 shows median lead time rose from 19 to 47–54 days. E2 and C1 show the DNA rate stepped from 8.1% to 13.4%, and C3 rules out seasonal and external rivals. Because the two exposures are perfectly collinear, neither causal effect can be identified separately. That rules out 'causal'. It does not erase the observed co-occurrence that 'association-only' describes. The key's answers follow directly from the stated semantics.
